Issued at 418 AM EST Wed Nov 11 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Pattern beginning to amplify across the continent as 160+kt upper 
jet buckles a bit over the Pacific. Ridging builds into the PacNW 
attm...while across the eastern/central US, troughing is beginning 
to deepen as a PV max digs from the Plains into the Mid MS 
valley...while at the same time, PV max over Manitoba sinks to the 
SSE, driven in part by lobe of energy swinging down through Hudson 
Bay on the back of a 526dam upper low over northern Quebec. Deepest 
moisture remains trapped across the southern US attm, though 
abundant Pacific moisture is filtering in upstream...and we do have 
some decent moisture in the Midwest ahead of the approaching system 
(pwats in the realm of 0.6 to 0.8in)....with weak stability aloft in 
the base of the trough over IA. Some deformation influences present 
over the Upper Midwest between the southward, cold advection 
progression of the Manitoba system and the subtle but weak 
northward, warm advection of the IA system...in the vicinity of 
baroclinic zone aloft that generally stretches from the Canadian 
Rockies down into the Great Lakes...though surface boundary still 
remains to our north attm (6z), attendant to the northern stream PV 
maxima...and much colder air to its north (-8 to -12C at 850mb 
across northern/central Manitoba/Ontario). Plains system continues 
to spin up as it moves into the Upper MS Valley, with warm front 
draped from northern MO into the OH Valley. Weak flow and 
radiational cooling across northern MI last evening resulted in some 
patchy fog, despite incoming mid/high clouds. 

System over the Plains will continue to trek ESE into the OH Valley 
today...as lobe of energy continues to dig down out of 
Ontario/Manitoba, crossing our region overnight. Additional lobes of 
energy swing through Thursday, reinforcing the cold air and 
encouraging a stronger pressure gradient over the region, with N to 
NE winds Thursday into Thursday night as upper low retrogrades 
toward James Bay/Ontario, likely becoming centered over the Lower 
Great Lakes and Mid-Atlantic/New England by Friday night. Surface 
high pressure will try to build in...but presence of the cold upper 
low over the warm lakes will keep parts of the Upper Great Lakes 
more unsettled right on into the weekend...perhaps finally clearing 
out by Saturday night and Sunday as a bit of cutoff energy crosses 
the southern US. After briefly stalling this weekend...the pattern 
will begin to move again as strong Pacific jet will keep things 
under motion. Appears the upstream pattern will amplify again next 
week...with troughing looking to deepen across the western US, 
forcing already strengthening ridge axis eastward across the Plains. 
Setup appears favorable for milder but active/unsettled weather to 
continue into early next week, depending on how close the storm 
track ends up to our neck of the woods. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/snow showers today through the rest of the week; accumulating 
snow Thursday night?.... The two systems sweeping in today should 
bring some showers to the area, though there is a reasonable chance, 
esp earlier in the day, for there to be two distinct areas of rain --
one associated with the northern stream feature, more likely over 
Lake Superior and the EUP, and a second along the confluence zone 
that should end up just to our south in central MI if current progs 
hold. As the system to our south passes, though, expecting an 
inverted surface trough to develop, which should strengthen 
somewhere over NW Lower, and will likely shift positions with time 
through tonight. The position of this lined up potentially down US-
131 from TC does signal some concerns for better convergence than 
expected over there, esp as temps continue to fall aloft...and winds 
eventually turning to the NE behind the inverted trough. Some snow 
could mix in, but still thinking the better chance for that will be 
Thursday night as the next more notable wave moves in with some 
deeper moisture and cooler temps aloft to enhance whatever light 
lake effect will be ongoing at that time. Still have concerns for N 
flow convergence bands to develop downwind of Grand Traverse Bay (as 
well as some of those north-facing nooks and crannies along the 
Leelanau Peninsula), signaling potential for higher QPF and 
snow/rainfall rates...particularly noting signals for decent amounts 
of low-level CAPE (especially over the lakes). Think this would be 
the best shot at accumulating snow across the area...where vigorous 
enough convection could overcome the warm soil temps, and a sloppy 
couple inches of snow could occur. Some prob guidance still hints at 
a 20-40 percent chance of 3 inches of snow Thursday night, and even 
assuming snow-to-liquid ratios remain low (sub-10-to-1), some of the 
higher QPF outputs (greater than a half inch of liquid equivalent in 
6hrs) do have me a bit concerned a few inches of snow could still 
occur
